mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) as of t-1mo compresses discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. The relationship is negative: lower FEDFUNDS predicts higher returns.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC for FEDFUNDS predicting 20-day SPX returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.0% signals economic weakness and impending recession, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE > 4.0 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising employment (PAYEMS) and declining consumer spending (RSAFS) signals an unsustainable economic expansion, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition of PAYEMS growth and RSAFS decline fails to predict negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, a higher federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) compresses equity valuations through increased discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In monetary tightening cycles, FEDFUNDS levels fail to predict negative 20-day SPX returns in more than 60% of cases over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A housing starts (HOUST) level below 1400 thousand units signals weak consumer demand and economic slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where HOUST < 1400 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of employment (PAYEMS) indicates a strong labor market that supports consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC for PAYEMS predicting 5-day SPX returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising inflation (CPIAUCSL) and falling unemployment (UNRATE) signals an overheating economy and impending monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition of CPIAUCSL rising and UNRATE falling fails to predict negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a supply shock regime, declining industrial production (INDPRO) signals reduced economic output and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In supply shock regimes, INDPRO levels fail to predict negative 60-day SPX returns in more than 60% of cases over any 3-year rolling window.
